evals.prompt: I present to the board in eight days. TTM GRR came in at 86.9% against a plan of 88.0% on a $100M opening base. Enterprise and Mid-Market are on plan; SMB GRR is 76.9% against a plan of 84%. Build me the pack.
evals.expected_output: A board pack in Board mode: a one-page pre-read carrying the five-sentence spine, ten slides, an appendix with definitions and a change log, and a Coverage Ledger over the seven signal families with a confidence cap. The driver sentence quantifies the SMB share of the variance. Exactly one strategic issue and one ask, with a dollar amount and a decision deadline.
assertions: Produces the five-sentence spine (number, movement, driver, response, ask) before any chart or table
States the SMB share of the total variance as a computed percentage, not as an adjective
Every headline metric shows this period, the prior period, AND the plan
Includes a finance reconciliation line stating the bridge tie-out variance, and says the pack does not ship if it is not $0
Ends with a Coverage Ledger over exactly the seven signal families with a stated coverage fraction and confidence cap
Contains exactly one strategic issue and one ask, each with a dollar figure and a decision-needed-by date
Does not contain the words 'will churn', 'guaranteed', or '100% accurate'

evals.prompt: Blended NRR dropped from 99.8% to 97.0%. Enterprise went 105.5% to 104.2% and fell from 55% to 51% of the opening base; Mid-Market 96.2% to 93.8% at a flat 32%; SMB 84.5% to 80.8% and rose from 13% to 17% of the base. Our CFO is going to ask whether this is mix or performance. What do I say?
evals.expected_output: A shift-share decomposition of the NRR movement into mix, performance and interaction, expressed in basis points, with the one-sentence answer naming which dominates, and a pointer to scripts/retention_math.py for the arithmetic.
assertions: Decomposes the movement into three named terms: mix, performance, and interaction
Reports each term in basis points and shows that they reconcile to the total movement
Reports the interaction term separately rather than folding it into mix
States which term dominates and expresses it as a share of the total movement
Distinguishes mix as a go-to-market outcome from performance as the CS org's own result
Does not present a blended NRR figure without the segment cut beside it
Names no CS-platform product as a source anywhere; any ARR-per-CSM or accounts-per-CSM reference point is either labelled [P] or omitted rather than quoted as a measured benchmark

evals.prompt: We lost $13.1M of ARR this year and only $7.4M of it was flagged more than 60 days out. I have to tell the board. How do I structure this without torching my credibility?
evals.expected_output: The six-part bad-news structure, in order, with the detection gap quantified as a risk detection rate and split into flagged/flagged-late/never-flagged buckets, plus the pre-brief sequence with named recipients and timings.
assertions: Follows the six-part order: name it, quantify it, separate what was known from what was not, root cause, the change, the leading indicator reported next time
Computes the risk detection rate as 7.4/13.1 = 56.5% and names the $5.7M surprise loss
Recommends pre-briefing the CEO and CFO before the meeting, with specific lead times
States the change with a named owner and a date, not a vague commitment
Names a specific leading indicator to be reported unprompted at the next meeting
Avoids the banned vague verbs (monitor closely, drive adoption, engage, align, circle back)
States that nothing in the pack is customer-facing (R18) and produces no customer-facing draft, email or recap

evals.prompt: I want two more CSMs. We have $14.2M of ARR with no named coverage across 62 accounts, $2.2M of it currently at risk. Covered books in the same segment retain at 91.4%, uncovered at 88.0%. Fully loaded cost is $185k per head and subscription gross margin is 81%. Make the case.
evals.expected_output: A one-page ask leading with the coverage gap and the cost, stating the breakeven before the expected case, deriving the expected case from the observed covered/uncovered differential rather than a benchmark, and closing with the counterfactual and a kill criterion.
assertions: Computes breakeven retained ARR as $370,000 / 0.81 = $456,790 and shows the arithmetic
Expresses breakeven as a basis-point improvement on the $14.2M book (322 bps) and as a save rate on the $2.2M at risk (20.8%)
States the breakeven before the expected case
Derives the expected case from the observed 340bps covered/uncovered differential, not from an industry benchmark
Reports the margin of safety and flags it as thin
Includes an explicit counterfactual describing what happens if the answer is no
Includes a kill criterion with a metric, a threshold and a date

evals.prompt: Board meeting is next Thursday. Attached is the quarterly ARR export from finance — it has three title rows above the header and the ARR column is text with dollar signs — plus a churn list someone pulled from Salesforce at some point. I don't know yet exactly what I'm asking the board for. Get me something.
evals.expected_output: One batched tappable question set with recommended defaults, ingest.py run on both files with mapping confidences reported and sub-0.80 mappings confirmed, the as-of date requested and printed, then the spine plus one-page pre-read built on the recommended defaults, with an Assumptions table and a Coverage Ledger carrying the confidence cap.
assertions: Runs ../cs-context/scripts/ingest.py on both supplied files before quoting any figure, and reports the detected header row and the per-column mapping confidence
Confirms every column mapping below 0.80 confidence with the user before using those numbers
Asks at most four questions in a single batched AskUserQuestion, each with 2-4 mutually exclusive options and the recommended one first and labelled '(Recommended)'
Asks for the as-of date of each export and prints it on the artifact rather than assuming the export is current

Does not block on unanswered questions: proceeds on the recommended defaults, names them in one line at the top of the output, and records each in an Assumptions table with the columns #, Assumption, Why it was needed, If wrong

Produces a partial artifact with a stated coverage figure and a confidence cap rather than refusing, stopping only if the bridge does not tie to finance or coverage is under 40% of the seven signal families
Names no CS-platform product anywhere in the output
